title: The summary for Monday 23 November
text:
Good morning, it is Monday 23 November: this is the GERICO summary.

In Ukraine, a Russian drone attack destroyed part of a five-storey building in Dymer, north of Kyiv. The governor of the region reports at least eleven dead. Rescuers are still searching for missing people, including two children. In the Kyiv region, Sunday's attacks killed at least fifteen people, according to Ukrainian authorities. President Zelensky asks the United States to deliver the Patriot missiles already paid for by the allies.

In Poland, the Lublin prosecutor's office confirms that the three objects that entered airspace on Friday were Russian cruise missiles. On Monday, the North Atlantic Council meets in Brussels.

In the Gulf, the Iran-aligned Houthis say they struck the Saudi refinery in Rabigh. The coalition led by Riyadh states it shot down a drone. President Trump says he could order new strikes against Iran next year if there is no agreement.

In Turkey, the UN climate conference ended without an agreement. The European Union and other countries rejected the text, which made no mention of fossil fuels.

Moving on to the markets. On Friday, Wall Street closed sharply down, with the Nasdaq dropping five point four per cent, the S&P 500 three point eight, and the Dow Jones two. Nvidia lost around thirteen per cent, following news of an SEC review of its accounting. European stock markets closed down on Friday: Milan by two point five per cent, Frankfurt by two point six, Paris by one point nine.

This morning, Asia is mixed. Seoul is down three per cent, after hitting a low of over five. Taipei is up two point five. Tokyo is closed for a holiday. Futures on the S&P 500 and the Nasdaq are up by more than two points.

On oil, Brent is at 92 dollars and WTI at 83, slightly down in early Asian trading. On Friday, gold was at $3,550, after losing more than nine per cent in a week. The spread between BTPs and Bunds closed on Friday at 110 basis points, and gas in Amsterdam at 88 euros per megawatt-hour.

On the Italian front, today the Budget Commission of the Chamber of Deputies carries out its initial assessment of the admissibility of the approximately seven thousand amendments to the budget.

Today's events. At 9:15, preliminary data on business activity are released in France, at 9:30 in Germany, at 10:00 in the euro area, and at 10:30 in the United Kingdom. At 15:45, it is the turn of the United States.

Full news, with sources, is on GERICO. No investment advice.
